spec_match.rationale: Each of the three omissions is demonstrated by its observable consequence — var() fallback reachability without initial-value, inheritance returning when inherits is dropped, and loss of interpolation with universal syntax — which is precisely the behavioural contract the CSSWG resolution describes.

interactive.rationale: Two test beds measure themselves on real elements at load with live verdicts and a summary table, and the Animate button runs a real transition sampling distinct computed values to show typed-vs-universal interpolation.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises three live test beds covering what dropping each descriptor gains and loses, including per-use var() fallbacks, and the page delivers exactly those three sections.

edge_cases.rationale: Every registration is wrapped and the pre-156 rejection path produces a detailed, honest explanation — including the subtle case where the child still inherits but only as an unregistered property, which the summary table labels 'yes, unregistered' rather than crediting the failed registration.

references.rationale: See-also links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5168674259468288 and the @property spec section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the same observable contracts this page measures (omissions accepted, fallback reachable, negatives unchanged); on Chromium 141 the route executed 4 pass / 4 fail, the expected pre-156 split, and the page's own verdicts agree with those results.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud session, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the load-time test beds genuinely ran — console showed the labelled '--gap-b rejected: SyntaxError' and '--label-c rejected: TypeError' warnings plus 'ready — 1/3 registrations accepted', and both screenshots show the honest rejection copy rendered — but the Animate interpolation comparison is click-driven and could not be exercised headlessly.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires 'omissions-measured' at load with accepted counts and 'interpolation-compared' after the animation, and the only console output is the page's own labelled logs — no unexpected errors.

design_system.rationale: Layout, cards and notes all use design-system variables and the button overrides both background and color, but .verdict.yes uses --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone (~3.7:1), below WCAG AA for its 0.85rem bold text; the rose 'no' state (~4.8:1) passes.

accessibility.rationale: Sections are labelled via aria-labelledby, per-section outcomes land in aria-live=polite outputs, the summary table has a caption and proper th scoping, and verdicts are conveyed as text rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px (headless shell) and 1280px: card pairs stack to one column on mobile, no horizontal overflow or clipped content, the Animate button meets 44px, and the same measured verdicts render on both classes.

openQuestions.title: Verdict colour semantics invert on the 'with initial-value' card
openQuestions.detail: On a 156+ browser the left card correctly reports 'fallback unreachable' and is styled with the rose .no class. That is the spec-correct outcome for a property that has an initial-value, so painting it as a failure state reads as if something is wrong with the browser. Consider a neutral third style (or copy such as 'fallback unreachable — as designed') so red is reserved for genuine failures.

openQuestions.title: Summary table omits the typed/universal interpolation pair
openQuestions.detail: The caption says 'What this browser did with each registration' but only --gap-a, --gap-b and --label-c are listed; --pad-typed and --pad-universal from the third test bed never get rows, and their 'interpolates' outcome is only visible in the section verdicts after clicking Animate. Pushing two more rows (updated after the animation runs) would make the summary complete.

openQuestions.title: Emerald verdict text misses WCAG AA on stone background
openQuestions.detail: Shared palette issue: --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone is ~3.7:1, below the 4.5:1 requirement for the 0.85rem bold verdict text (invariant #5). Same finding as the sibling descriptor-lab page; likely wants a palette-level decision rather than per-page hex.

summary: The strongest page in this feature's portfolio: it measures, on real elements, what each descriptor omission actually changes — fallback reachability, inheritance, and interpolation — and it auto-runs two of its three test beds at load, which made genuine runtime verification possible even in this headless session. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/optional-descriptors-for-registered-custom-properties/what-each-omission-buys/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, console showing only the page's labelled pre-156 rejection warnings, feature /conformance/ route at 4 pass / 4 fail as expected for this browser). On this 141 build the page correctly reported the SyntaxError/TypeError rejections with copy explaining that this is the pre-Chrome-156 rule, and even distinguished unregistered inheritance from registered inheritance in the summary table. Remaining questions are presentational: verdict colour semantics, a summary table that misses the interpolation pair, and the shared emerald-on-stone contrast shortfall.
